body.statement: For the exact four-relation transition system, can one prove that every irreducible residual token has a verifier-accepted candidate: either a projection circuit whose cross-multiplied target identity holds on \(\mathcal I_H\), or a signed canonical-row contrast whose rational box lifts through all interacting districts, fixed kernels, and observed descendants while preserving every supported observed cell and exactly \(H\)? The proof must also exclude an identified residual whose only identifying functional is nonrational.
body.justification: This is the genuine open content: local contextwise witnesses do not automatically couple across shared selector gates and interacting districts.
body.gap: Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser explicitly conjecture completeness; Kivva and coauthors solve a different positivity-qualified gID reduction, and no searched paper supplies this fixed-support residual alternative.
body.consumer: Resolving the dichotomy yields a decision procedure that never invents an unsupplied experimental regime and explains every failure by an exact global pair.
